passages.original: Stand back; room! bear back.
passages.vernacular: 後退;讓出地方!往後退。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 後退;讓出地方!往後退。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: If you have tears, prepare to shed them now. You all do know this mantle. I remember The first time ever Caesar put it on; ’Twas on a Summer’s evening, in his tent, That day he overcame the Nervii. Look, in this place ran Cassius’ dagger through: See what a rent the envious Casca made: Through this the well-beloved Brutus stabb’d; And as he pluck’d his cursed steel away, Mark how the blood of Caesar follow’d it, As rushing out of doors, to be resolv’d If Brutus so unkindly knock’d, or no; For Brutus, as you know, was Caesar’s angel. Judge, O you gods, how dearly Caesar lov’d him. This was the most unkindest cut of all; For when the noble Caesar saw him stab, Ingratitude, more strong than traitors’ arms, Quite vanquish’d him: then burst his mighty heart; And in his mantle muffling up his face, Even at the base of Pompey’s statue Which all the while ran blood, great Caesar fell. O, what a fall was there, my countrymen! Then I, and you, and all of us fell down, Whilst bloody treason flourish’d over us. O, now you weep; and I perceive you feel The dint of pity. These are gracious drops. Kind souls, what weep you when you but behold Our Caesar’s vesture wounded? Look you here, Here is himself, marr’d, as you see, with traitors.
passages.vernacular: 如果你哋有眼淚,準備而家流吧。你哋都認得呢件斗篷。我記得凱撒第一次穿上佢嘅時候;嗰個係夏天嘅傍晚,喺佢嘅帳篷裡,就係佢打敗納爾維人嗰天。睇,喺呢度卡修斯嘅匕首刺穿喇:睇嫉妒嘅卡斯卡撕開咗點樣嘅口子:從呢度,深受愛戴嘅布魯圖斯刺咗進去;當佢拔出佢該詛咒嘅鋼刃,注意凱撒嘅血點樣跟住佢出嚟,彷彿衝出門外,要確認布魯圖斯係咪咁樣無情地敲門;因為布魯圖斯,你哋知道,係凱撒嘅天使。諸神啊,請判斷凱撒幾咁深愛佢。呢個係所有刺傷中最無情嘅;因為當高貴嘅凱撒睇見佢刺,比叛徒嘅手臂更強嘅忘恩負義完全壓垮咗佢:然後佢強大嘅心破裂;佢用斗篷蒙住臉,就喺龐培雕像嘅底座旁,嗰雕像一直喺流血,偉大嘅凱撒倒下喇。啊,嗰個係點樣嘅一倒,我嘅同胞哋!於是我,同你哋,同我哋所有人都倒下喇,而血腥嘅叛逆喺我哋頭上昌盛。啊,而家你哋哭喇;我睇出你哋感受到憐憫嘅打擊。呢個係善良嘅淚珠。善良嘅靈魂,你哋只係睇到我哋凱撒嘅衣服受傷就哭咗嗎?睇呢度,呢個係佢本人,如你哋所見,被叛徒毀壞喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你們有眼淚,準備現在流吧。你們都認得這件斗篷。我記得凱撒第一次穿上它的時候;那是夏天的傍晚,在他的帳篷裡,就是他打敗納爾維人那天。看,在這裡卡修斯的匕首刺穿了:看嫉妒的卡斯卡撕開了怎樣的口子:從這裡,深受愛戴的布魯圖斯刺了進去;當他拔出他該詛咒的鋼刃,注意凱撒的血怎樣跟著它出來,彷彿衝出門外,要確認布魯圖斯是否這樣無情地敲門;因為布魯圖斯,你們知道,是凱撒的天使。諸神啊,請判斷凱撒多麼深愛他。這是所有刺傷中最無情的;因為當高貴的凱撒看見他刺,比叛徒的手臂更強的忘恩負義完全壓垮了他:然後他強大的心破裂;他用斗篷蒙住臉,就在龐培雕像的底座旁,那雕像一直在流血,偉大的凱撒倒下了。啊,那是怎樣的一倒,我的同胞們!於是我,和你們,和我們所有人都倒下了,而血腥的叛逆在我們頭上昌盛。啊,現在你們哭了;我看出你們感受到憐憫的打擊。這是善良的淚珠。善良的靈魂,你們只是看到我們凱撒的衣服受傷就哭了嗎?看這裡,這是他本人,如你們所見,被叛徒毀壞了。

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: O piteous spectacle!
passages.vernacular: 啊可憐嘅景象!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊可憐的景象!

passages.title: Second Citizen 第二市民
passages.original: O noble Caesar!
passages.vernacular: 啊高貴嘅凱撒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊高貴的凱撒!

passages.title: Third Citizen 第三市民
passages.original: O woeful day!
passages.vernacular: 啊悲哀嘅一天!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊悲哀的一天!

passages.title: Fourth Citizen 第四市民
passages.original: O traitors, villains!
passages.vernacular: 啊叛徒,惡棍!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊叛徒,惡棍!

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: O most bloody sight!
passages.vernacular: 啊最血腥嘅景象!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊最血腥的景象!

passages.title: Second Citizen 第二市民
passages.original: We will be revenged.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要報仇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要報仇。

passages.title: Citizens 市民們
passages.original: Revenge,—about,—seek,—burn,—fire,—kill,—slay,—let not a traitor live!
passages.vernacular: 報仇,——動手,——搜,——燒,——放火,——殺,——砍,——唔好畀一個叛徒活!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 報仇,——動手,——搜,——燒,——放火,——殺,——砍,——別讓一個叛徒活!

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Stay, countrymen.
passages.vernacular: 留下,同胞哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 留下,同胞們。

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: Peace there! Hear the noble Antony.
passages.vernacular: 安靜!聽高貴嘅安東尼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安靜!聽高貴的安東尼。

passages.title: Second Citizen 第二市民
passages.original: We’ll hear him, we’ll follow him, we’ll die with him.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要聽佢,我哋要跟隨佢,我哋要同佢同死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要聽他,我們要跟隨他,我們要與他同死。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Good friends, sweet friends, let me not stir you up To such a sudden flood of mutiny. They that have done this deed are honourable. What private griefs they have, alas, I know not, That made them do it. They’re wise and honourable, And will, no doubt, with reasons answer you. I come not, friends, to steal away your hearts. I am no orator, as Brutus is; But, as you know me all, a plain blunt man, That love my friend; and that they know full well That gave me public leave to speak of him. For I have neither wit, nor words, nor worth, Action, nor utterance, nor the power of speech, To stir men’s blood. I only speak right on. I tell you that which you yourselves do know, Show you sweet Caesar’s wounds, poor poor dumb mouths, And bid them speak for me. But were I Brutus, And Brutus Antony, there were an Antony Would ruffle up your spirits, and put a tongue In every wound of Caesar, that should move The stones of Rome to rise and mutiny.
passages.vernacular: 好朋友哋,親愛嘅朋友哋,唔好畀我把你哋激到咁樣突然嘅暴動洪流。做呢件事嘅人係可敬嘅。佢哋有乜嘢私人嘅悲痛,唉,我唔知道,使佢哋咁樣做。佢哋聰明而可敬,無疑會用理由回答你哋。朋友哋,我嚟唔係要偷走你哋嘅心。我唔係演講家,像布魯圖斯嗰樣;但正如你哋都認識我,係個樸實直率嘅人,愛我嘅朋友;嗰啲畀我公開許可講佢嘅人好清楚呢啲。因為我既冇機智,都冇言辭,都冇身分、姿態、口才或言語嘅力量,去激動人哋嘅血。我只係直講。我告訴你哋你哋自己知道嘅事,畀你哋睇親愛嘅凱撒嘅傷口,可憐嘅、可憐嘅啞口,叫佢哋替我講話。但如果我係布魯圖斯,而布魯圖斯係安東尼,就會有一個安東尼,能激起你哋嘅精神,喺凱撒嘅每一道傷口裡放一條舌頭,動搖羅馬嘅石頭起嚟暴動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好朋友們,親愛的朋友們,別讓我把你們激到這樣突然的暴動洪流。做這件事的人是可敬的。他們有什麼私人的悲痛,唉,我不知道,使他們這樣做。他們聰明而可敬,無疑會用理由回答你們。朋友們,我來不是要偷走你們的心。我不是演說家,像布魯圖斯那樣;但正如你們都認識我,是個樸實直率的人,愛我的朋友;那些給我公開許可說他的人很清楚這一點。因為我既沒有機智,也沒有言辭,也沒有身分、姿態、口才或言語的力量,去激動人們的血。我只是直說。我告訴你們你們自己知道的事,給你們看親愛的凱撒的傷口,可憐的、可憐的啞口,叫它們替我說話。但如果我是布魯圖斯,而布魯圖斯是安東尼,就會有一個安東尼,能激起你們的精神,在凱撒的每一道傷口裡放一條舌頭,動搖羅馬的石頭起來暴動。

passages.title: Citizens 市民們
passages.original: We’ll mutiny.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要暴動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要暴動。

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: We’ll burn the house of Brutus.
passages.vernacular: 我哋要燒布魯圖斯嘅房子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們要燒布魯圖斯的房子。

passages.title: Third Citizen 第三市民
passages.original: Away, then! come, seek the conspirators.
passages.vernacular: 嗰就走!嚟,搜捕陰謀者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那就走!來,搜捕陰謀者。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Yet hear me, countrymen; yet hear me speak.
passages.vernacular: 定係聽我講,同胞哋;定係聽我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是聽我說,同胞們;還是聽我說。

passages.title: Citizens 市民們
passages.original: Peace, ho! Hear Antony; most noble Antony.
passages.vernacular: 安靜,喂!聽安東尼;最高貴嘅安東尼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安靜,喂!聽安東尼;最高貴的安東尼。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Why, friends, you go to do you know not what. Wherein hath Caesar thus deserved your loves? Alas, you know not; I must tell you then. You have forgot the will I told you of.
passages.vernacular: 哎,朋友哋,你哋去做你哋唔知道嘅事。凱撒喺邊方面咁樣值得你哋嘅愛?唉,你哋唔知道;嗰我必須告訴你哋。你哋忘咗我講嘅遺囑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,朋友們,你們去做你們不知道的事。凱撒在哪方面這樣值得你們的愛?唉,你們不知道;那我必須告訴你們。你們忘了我說的遺囑。

passages.title: Citizens 市民們
passages.original: Most true; the will!—let’s stay, and hear the will.
passages.vernacular: 最對;遺囑!——我哋留下,聽遺囑。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最對;遺囑!——我們留下,聽遺囑。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Here is the will, and under Caesar’s seal. To every Roman citizen he gives, To every several man, seventy-five drachmas.
passages.vernacular: 呢度係遺囑,蓋住凱撒嘅印。佢畀每個羅馬公民,畀每一個人,七十五德拉克馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這裡是遺囑,蓋著凱撒的印。他給每個羅馬公民,給每一個人,七十五德拉克馬。

passages.title: Second Citizen 第二市民
passages.original: Most noble Caesar! We’ll revenge his death.
passages.vernacular: 最高貴嘅凱撒!我哋要為佢嘅死報仇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最高貴的凱撒!我們要為他的死報仇。

passages.title: Third Citizen 第三市民
passages.original: O, royal Caesar!
passages.vernacular: 啊,帝王般嘅凱撒!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,帝王般的凱撒!

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Hear me with patience.
passages.vernacular: 耐心聽我講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 耐心聽我說。

passages.title: Citizens 市民們
passages.original: Peace, ho!
passages.vernacular: 安靜,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安靜,喂!

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Moreover, he hath left you all his walks, His private arbors, and new-planted orchards, On this side Tiber; he hath left them you, And to your heirs forever; common pleasures, To walk abroad, and recreate yourselves. Here was a Caesar! when comes such another?
passages.vernacular: 此外,佢把佢所有嘅散步道、私人涼亭同新種嘅果園,喺台伯河呢邊,都留畀你哋;佢把佢哋留畀你哋,同你哋嘅子孫,永遠;公共嘅樂趣,供你哋出去散步、消遣。呢個就係一位凱撒!乜嘢時候仲會有咁樣嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 此外,他把他所有的散步道、私人涼亭和新種的果園,在台伯河這邊,都留給你們;他把它們留給你們,和你們的子孫,永遠;公共的樂趣,供你們出去散步、消遣。這就是一位凱撒!什麼時候還會有這樣的?

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: Never, never. Come, away, away! We’ll burn his body in the holy place, And with the brands fire the traitors’ houses. Take up the body.
passages.vernacular: 永遠唔會,永遠唔會。嚟,走,走!我哋要喺聖地焚燒佢嘅遺體,用火把點燃叛徒嘅房子。抬起遺體。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 永遠不會,永遠不會。來,走,走!我們要在聖地焚燒他的遺體,用火把點燃叛徒的房子。抬起遺體。

passages.title: Second Citizen 第二市民
passages.original: Go, fetch fire.
passages.vernacular: 去,攞火嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去,拿火來。

passages.title: Third Citizen 第三市民
passages.original: Pluck down benches.
passages.vernacular: 拆下長凳。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拆下長凳。

passages.title: Fourth Citizen 第四市民
passages.original: Pluck down forms, windows, anything.
passages.vernacular: 拆下長椅、窗戶,乜嘢都拆。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 拆下長椅、窗戶,什麼都拆。

passages.original: [Exeunt Citizens, with the body.]
passages.vernacular: [市民哋抬住遺體下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [市民們抬著遺體下。]

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Now let it work. Mischief, thou art afoot, Take thou what course thou wilt!
passages.vernacular: 而家讓佢發揮作用。禍害,你已起步,愛走邊條路就走邊條!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在讓它發揮作用。禍害,你已起步,愛走哪條路就走哪條!

passages.original: Enter a Servant.
passages.vernacular: [一名僕人上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一名僕人上。]

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: How now, fellow?
passages.vernacular: 點喇,朋友?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,朋友?

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: Sir, Octavius is already come to Rome.
passages.vernacular: 先生,屋大維已經嚟到羅馬。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生,屋大維已經來到羅馬。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Where is he?
passages.vernacular: 佢喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他在哪裡?

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: He and Lepidus are at Caesar’s house.
passages.vernacular: 佢同雷必達喺凱撒家。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他和雷必達在凱撒家。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: And thither will I straight to visit him. He comes upon a wish. Fortune is merry, And in this mood will give us anything.
passages.vernacular: 我即刻就到嗰度去探望佢。佢嚟得正合心意。命運喺歡樂,喺呢種心情下會畀我哋任何嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我馬上就到那裡去探望他。他來得正合心意。命運在歡樂,在這種心情下會給我們任何東西。

passages.title: Servant 僕人
passages.original: I heard him say Brutus and Cassius Are rid like madmen through the gates of Rome.
passages.vernacular: 我聽佢講布魯圖斯同卡修斯像瘋子一樣騎馬穿過羅馬嘅城門。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我聽他說布魯圖斯和卡修斯像瘋子一樣騎馬穿過羅馬的城門。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Belike they had some notice of the people, How I had moved them. Bring me to Octavius.
passages.vernacular: 大概佢哋得到咗關於人民嘅啲消息,關於我點樣感動佢哋。帶我去屋大維嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大概他們得到了關於人民的一些消息,關於我怎樣感動他們。帶我去屋大維那裡。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act III, Scene III — A Street 第三幕第三場:街道

passages.original: Enter Cinna, the poet, and after him the citizens.
passages.vernacular: [詩人辛納上,市民哋跟隨其後。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [詩人辛納上,市民們跟隨其後。]

passages.title: Cinna 辛納
passages.original: I dreamt tonight that I did feast with Caesar, And things unluckily charge my fantasy. I have no will to wander forth of doors, Yet something leads me forth.
passages.vernacular: 我今晚夢見自己同凱撒共宴,不吉利嘅事纏住我嘅幻想。我冇意願到外面遊蕩,不過有乜嘢嘢領我出嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我今晚夢見自己與凱撒共宴,不吉利的事纏著我的幻想。我沒有意願到外面遊蕩,可是有什麼東西領我出來。

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: What is your name?
passages.vernacular: 你叫乜嘢名字?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你叫什麼名字?

passages.title: Second Citizen 第二市民
passages.original: Whither are you going?
passages.vernacular: 你往邊度去?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你往哪裡去?

passages.title: Third Citizen 第三市民
passages.original: Where do you dwell?
passages.vernacular: 你住喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你住在哪裡?

passages.title: Fourth Citizen 第四市民
passages.original: Are you a married man or a bachelor?
passages.vernacular: 你係已婚定係單身?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你是已婚還是單身?

passages.title: Second Citizen 第二市民
passages.original: Answer every man directly.
passages.vernacular: 直接回答每一個人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直接回答每一個人。

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: Ay, and briefly.
passages.vernacular: 對,而且要簡短。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,而且要簡短。

passages.title: Fourth Citizen 第四市民
passages.original: Ay, and wisely.
passages.vernacular: 對,而且要聰明。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,而且要聰明。

passages.title: Third Citizen 第三市民
passages.original: Ay, and truly, you were best.
passages.vernacular: 對,而且要老實,你最好咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對,而且要老實,你最好這樣。

passages.title: Cinna 辛納
passages.original: What is my name? Whither am I going? Where do I dwell? Am I a married man or a bachelor? Then, to answer every man directly and briefly, wisely and truly. Wisely I say I am a bachelor.
passages.vernacular: 我叫乜嘢名字?我往邊度去?我住喺邊度?我係已婚定係單身?咁,直接簡短、聰明老實地回答每一個人。聰明地講,我係單身。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我叫什麼名字?我往哪裡去?我住在哪裡?我是已婚還是單身?那麼,直接簡短、聰明老實地回答每一個人。聰明地說,我是單身。

passages.title: Second Citizen 第二市民
passages.original: That’s as much as to say they are fools that marry; you’ll bear me a bang for that, I fear. Proceed, directly.
passages.vernacular: 嗰等於講結婚嘅人係傻瓜;你為此要挨我一拳,我怕。繼續,直接講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那等於說結婚的人是傻瓜;你為此要挨我一拳,我怕。繼續,直接說。

passages.title: Cinna 辛納
passages.original: Directly, I am going to Caesar’s funeral.
passages.vernacular: 直接講,我去凱撒嘅葬禮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 直接說,我去凱撒的葬禮。

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: As a friend, or an enemy?
passages.vernacular: 以朋友定係敵人嘅身分?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以朋友還是敵人的身分?

passages.title: Cinna 辛納
passages.original: As a friend.
passages.vernacular: 以朋友嘅身分。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以朋友的身分。

passages.title: Second Citizen 第二市民
passages.original: That matter is answered directly.
passages.vernacular: 呢個問題直接回答喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這個問題直接回答了。

passages.title: Fourth Citizen 第四市民
passages.original: For your dwelling, briefly.
passages.vernacular: 關於你嘅住處,簡短講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 關於你的住處,簡短說。

passages.title: Cinna 辛納
passages.original: Briefly, I dwell by the Capitol.
passages.vernacular: 簡短講,我住喺神殿旁。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 簡短說,我住在神殿旁。

passages.title: Third Citizen 第三市民
passages.original: Your name, sir, truly.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅名字,先生,老實講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的名字,先生,老實說。

passages.title: Cinna 辛納
passages.original: Truly, my name is Cinna.
passages.vernacular: 老實講,我嘅名字係辛納。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 老實說,我的名字是辛納。

passages.title: First Citizen 第一市民
passages.original: Tear him to pieces! He’s a conspirator.
passages.vernacular: 把佢撕成碎片!佢係陰謀者。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把他撕成碎片!他是陰謀者。

passages.title: Cinna 辛納
passages.original: I am Cinna the poet, I am Cinna the poet.
passages.vernacular: 我係詩人辛納,我係詩人辛納。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是詩人辛納,我是詩人辛納。

passages.title: Fourth Citizen 第四市民
passages.original: Tear him for his bad verses, tear him for his bad verses.
passages.vernacular: 為佢嘅壞詩撕咗佢,為佢嘅壞詩撕咗佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 為他的壞詩撕了他,為他的壞詩撕了他。

passages.title: Cinna 辛納
passages.original: I am not Cinna the conspirator.
passages.vernacular: 我唔係陰謀者辛納。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是陰謀者辛納。

passages.title: Fourth Citizen 第四市民
passages.original: It is no matter, his name’s Cinna; pluck but his name out of his heart, and turn him going.
passages.vernacular: 冇關係,佢嘅名字叫辛納;只要把佢嘅名字從佢心裡拔出嚟,把佢打發走。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒關係,他的名字叫辛納;只要把他的名字從他心裡拔出來,把他打發走。

passages.title: Third Citizen 第三市民
passages.original: Tear him, tear him! Come; brands, ho! firebrands. To Brutus’, to Cassius’; burn all. Some to Decius’ house, and some to Casca’s, some to Ligarius’. Away, go!
passages.vernacular: 撕佢,撕佢!嚟;火把,喂!火把。去布魯圖斯家,去卡修斯家;全燒掉。有些去狄修斯家,有些去卡斯卡家,有些去利加留斯家。走,去!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 撕他,撕他!來;火把,喂!火把。去布魯圖斯家,去卡修斯家;全燒掉。有些去狄修斯家,有些去卡斯卡家,有些去利加留斯家。走,去!

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene I — Rome. A Room in Antony’s House 第四幕第一場:羅馬,安東尼家一室

passages.original: Enter Antony, Octavius and Lepidus, seated at a table.
passages.vernacular: [安東尼、屋大維同雷必達坐喺桌旁上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [安東尼、屋大維與雷必達坐在桌旁上。]

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: These many then shall die; their names are prick’d.
passages.vernacular: 呢啲人就要死;佢哋嘅名字已被點出。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這些人就要死;他們的名字已被點出。

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: Your brother too must die; consent you, Lepidus?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅兄弟都必須死;你同意嗎,雷必達?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的兄弟也必須死;你同意嗎,雷必達?

passages.title: Lepidus 雷必達
passages.original: I do consent,—
passages.vernacular: 我同意,——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我同意,——

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: Prick him down, Antony.
passages.vernacular: 把佢劃掉,安東尼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把他劃掉,安東尼。

passages.title: Lepidus 雷必達
passages.original: Upon condition Publius shall not live, Who is your sister’s son, Mark Antony.
passages.vernacular: 條件係帕布利烏斯唔能夠活,佢係你姊姊嘅兒子,馬克·安東尼。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 條件是帕布利烏斯不能活,他是你姊姊的兒子,馬克·安東尼。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: He shall not live; look, with a spot I damn him. But, Lepidus, go you to Caesar’s house; Fetch the will hither, and we shall determine How to cut off some charge in legacies.
passages.vernacular: 佢唔能夠活;睇,我用一個點判佢死。但係,雷必達,你去凱撒家;把遺囑攞嚟呢度,我哋將決定如何削減遺贈中嘅啲費用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他不能活;看,我用一個點判他死。但是,雷必達,你去凱撒家;把遺囑拿來這裡,我們將決定如何削減遺贈中的一些費用。

passages.title: Lepidus 雷必達
passages.original: What, shall I find you here?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,我會喺呢度找到你哋嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,我會在這裡找到你們嗎?

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: Or here, or at the Capitol.
passages.vernacular: 要麼呢度,要麼喺神殿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 要麼這裡,要麼在神殿。

passages.original: [Exit Lepidus.]
passages.vernacular: [雷必達下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [雷必達下。]

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: This is a slight unmeritable man, Meet to be sent on errands. Is it fit, The three-fold world divided, he should stand One of the three to share it?
passages.vernacular: 呢個係個微不足道、無功績嘅人,適合被派去跑腿。三分嘅世界被分開喇,佢適合站喺三人之一去分享嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是個微不足道、無功績的人,適合被派去跑腿。三分的世界被分開了,他適合站在三人之一去分享嗎?

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: So you thought him, And took his voice who should be prick’d to die In our black sentence and proscription.
passages.vernacular: 你原來咁樣認為佢,並採用佢嘅意見決定邊個該喺我哋黑色嘅判決同放逐令中被點出去死。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你原來這樣認為他,並採用他的意見決定誰該在我們黑色的判決和放逐令中被點出去死。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Octavius, I have seen more days than you; And though we lay these honours on this man, To ease ourselves of divers sland’rous loads, He shall but bear them as the ass bears gold, To groan and sweat under the business, Either led or driven, as we point the way; And having brought our treasure where we will, Then take we down his load, and turn him off, Like to the empty ass, to shake his ears, And graze in commons.
passages.vernacular: 屋大維,我比你見過更多日子;雖然我哋把呢啲榮譽加喺呢個人身上,為了減輕我哋各種受誹謗嘅負擔,佢只會像驢馱金子一樣背住佢哋,喺差事下呻吟流汗,或被牽或被趕,隨我哋指路;把我哋嘅財寶運到我哋想去嘅地方後,我哋就卸下佢嘅負擔,把佢像空驢子一樣趕走,抖抖耳朵,到公地食草。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 屋大維,我比你見過更多日子;雖然我們把這些榮譽加在這個人身上,為了減輕我們各種受誹謗的負擔,他只會像驢馱金子一樣背著它們,在差事下呻吟流汗,或被牽或被趕,隨我們指路;把我們的財寶運到我們想去的地方後,我們就卸下他的負擔,把他像空驢子一樣趕走,抖抖耳朵,到公地吃草。

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: You may do your will; But he’s a tried and valiant soldier.
passages.vernacular: 你可以隨意;但佢係個久經考驗嘅勇敢軍人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你可以隨意;但他是個久經考驗的勇敢軍人。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: So is my horse, Octavius; and for that I do appoint him store of provender. It is a creature that I teach to fight, To wind, to stop, to run directly on, His corporal motion govern’d by my spirit. And, in some taste, is Lepidus but so: He must be taught, and train’d, and bid go forth: A barren-spirited fellow; one that feeds On objects, arts, and imitations, Which, out of use and stal’d by other men, Begin his fashion. Do not talk of him But as a property. And now, Octavius, Listen great things. Brutus and Cassius Are levying powers; we must straight make head. Therefore let our alliance be combin’d, Our best friends made, our means stretch’d; And let us presently go sit in council, How covert matters may be best disclos’d, And open perils surest answered.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅馬都係,屋大維;因此我畀牠安排大量飼料。呢個係我教牠打仗、轉彎、止步、直衝嘅生物,牠身體嘅動作受我嘅精神支配。喺某種程度上,雷必達都不過如此:佢必須被教導、被訓練、被吩咐前進:一個精神貧瘠嘅人;靠對象、技藝同模仿為生,嗰啲嘢被別人用舊、不新鮮喇,才成為佢嘅時尚。唔好把佢講成別嘅,只當成一件工具。而家,屋大維,聽大事。布魯圖斯同卡修斯正在徵集兵力;我哋必須即刻對抗。所以讓我哋嘅聯盟聯合起嚟,結好我哋最好嘅朋友,延展我哋嘅手段;讓我哋即刻去開會商議,如何最好地揭露隱秘嘅事,並最穩妥地應對公開嘅危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的馬也是,屋大維;因此我給牠安排大量飼料。這是我教牠打仗、轉彎、止步、直衝的生物,牠身體的動作受我的精神支配。在某種程度上,雷必達也不過如此:他必須被教導、被訓練、被吩咐前進:一個精神貧瘠的人;靠對象、技藝和模仿為生,那些東西被別人用舊、不新鮮了,才成為他的時尚。不要把他說成別的,只當成一件工具。現在,屋大維,聽大事。布魯圖斯和卡修斯正在徵集兵力;我們必須馬上對抗。所以讓我們的聯盟聯合起來,結好我們最好的朋友,延展我們的手段;讓我們馬上去開會商議,如何最好地揭露隱秘的事,並最穩妥地應對公開的危險。

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: Let us do so: for we are at the stake, And bay’d about with many enemies; And some that smile have in their hearts, I fear, Millions of mischiefs.
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣做:因為我哋被逼到死角,被許多敵人圍困;有些微笑嘅人,我怕,心裡有百萬種惡意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣做:因為我們被逼到死角,被許多敵人圍困;有些微笑的人,我怕,心裡有百萬種惡意。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene II — Before Brutus’ Tent, near Sardis 第四幕第二場:薩迪斯附近,布魯圖斯營帳前

passages.original: Drum. Enter Brutus, Lucilius, Titinius and Soldiers; Pindarus meeting them; Lucius at some distance.
passages.vernacular: [鼓聲。布魯圖斯、魯西留斯、提提紐斯同士兵哋上;平達魯斯同佢哋相遇;路修斯喺遠處。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [鼓聲。布魯圖斯、魯西留斯、提提紐斯與士兵們上;平達魯斯與他們相遇;路修斯在遠處。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Stand, ho!
passages.vernacular: 站住,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站住,喂!

passages.title: Lucilius 魯西留斯
passages.original: Give the word, ho! and stand.
passages.vernacular: 傳口令,喂!站住。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 傳口令,喂!站住。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: What now, Lucilius! is Cassius near?
passages.vernacular: 點喇,魯西留斯!卡修斯近咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了,魯西留斯!卡修斯近了嗎?

passages.title: Lucilius 魯西留斯
passages.original: He is at hand, and Pindarus is come To do you salutation from his master.
passages.vernacular: 佢就喺附近,平達魯斯嚟向你致敬,代表佢嘅主人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他就在附近,平達魯斯來向你致敬,代表他的主人。

passages.original: [Pindarus gives a letter to Brutus.]
passages.vernacular: [平達魯斯交一封信畀布魯圖斯。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [平達魯斯交一封信給布魯圖斯。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: He greets me well. Your master, Pindarus, In his own change, or by ill officers, Hath given me some worthy cause to wish Things done, undone: but, if he be at hand, I shall be satisfied.
passages.vernacular: 佢向我致意得好好。你嘅主人,平達魯斯,出於佢自己嘅改變,或由於壞下屬,畀咗我啲值得嘅理由,使我希望有些事做成咗又撤銷:但係,若佢就喺附近,我會得到解釋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他向我致意得很好。你的主人,平達魯斯,出於他自己的改變,或由於壞下屬,給了我一些值得的理由,使我希望有些事做成了又撤銷:但是,若他就在附近,我會得到解釋。

passages.title: Pindarus 平達魯斯
passages.original: I do not doubt But that my noble master will appear Such as he is, full of regard and honour.
passages.vernacular: 我不懷疑我高貴嘅主人會表現得係佢本來嘅樣子,充滿敬意同榮譽。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不懷疑我高貴的主人會表現得是他本來的樣子,充滿敬意和榮譽。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: He is not doubted. A word, Lucilius; How he received you, let me be resolv’d.
passages.vernacular: 佢冇被懷疑。魯西留斯,講句話;佢點樣接待你,讓我弄清楚。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他沒有被懷疑。魯西留斯,說句話;他怎樣接待你,讓我弄清楚。

passages.title: Lucilius 魯西留斯
passages.original: With courtesy and with respect enough, But not with such familiar instances, Nor with such free and friendly conference, As he hath us’d of old.
passages.vernacular: 以足夠嘅禮貌同尊重,但冇以往嗰種親密嘅表現,都冇嗰種自由友好嘅交談,像佢往日所用嘅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 以足夠的禮貌和尊重,但沒有以往那種親密的表現,也沒有那種自由友好的交談,像他往日所用的。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Thou hast describ’d A hot friend cooling. Ever note, Lucilius, When love begins to sicken and decay It useth an enforced ceremony. There are no tricks in plain and simple faith; But hollow men, like horses hot at hand, Make gallant show and promise of their mettle;
passages.vernacular: 你描述嘅係一位熱情嘅朋友喺變冷。魯西留斯,永遠記住,當愛開始生病衰退,佢就使用勉強嘅禮節。純樸單一嘅信義中冇把戲;但空心嘅人,像喺手邊發熱嘅馬,擺出英勇嘅樣子同對其勇氣嘅承諾;
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你描述的是一位熱情的朋友在變冷。魯西留斯,永遠記住,當愛開始生病衰退,它就使用勉強的禮節。純樸單一的信義中沒有把戲;但空心的人,像在手邊發熱的馬,擺出英勇的樣子和對其勇氣的承諾;

passages.original: [Low march within.]
passages.vernacular: [內有低沉嘅行軍聲。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [內有低沉的行軍聲。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: But when they should endure the bloody spur, They fall their crests, and like deceitful jades Sink in the trial. Comes his army on?
passages.vernacular: 但當佢哋該忍受血腥嘅馬刺時,佢哋垂下鬃毛,像欺人嘅劣馬,喺考驗中倒下。佢嘅軍隊嚟咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 但當它們該忍受血腥的馬刺時,它們垂下鬃毛,像欺人的劣馬,在考驗中倒下。他的軍隊來了嗎?

passages.title: Lucilius 魯西留斯
passages.original: They meant this night in Sardis to be quarter’d; The greater part, the horse in general, Are come with Cassius.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋打算今晚駐紮喺薩迪斯;大部分,全部騎兵,同卡修斯一同嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們打算今晚駐紮在薩迪斯;大部分,全部騎兵,與卡修斯一同來。

passages.original: Enter Cassius and Soldiers.
passages.vernacular: [卡修斯同士兵哋上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [卡修斯與士兵們上。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Hark! he is arriv’d. March gently on to meet him.
passages.vernacular: 聽!佢到喇。慢慢前進迎接佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽!他到了。慢慢前進迎接他。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Stand, ho!
passages.vernacular: 站住,喂!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站住,喂!

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Stand, ho! Speak the word along.
passages.vernacular: 站住,喂!沿路傳口令。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站住,喂!沿路傳口令。

passages.title: First Soldier 第一士兵
passages.original: Stand!
passages.vernacular: 站住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站住!

passages.title: Second Soldier 第二士兵
passages.original: Stand!
passages.vernacular: 站住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站住!

passages.title: Third Soldier 第三士兵
passages.original: Stand!
passages.vernacular: 站住!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 站住!

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Most noble brother, you have done me wrong.
passages.vernacular: 最高貴嘅兄弟,你冤枉咗我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 最高貴的兄弟,你冤枉了我。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Judge me, you gods; wrong I mine enemies? And if not so, how should I wrong a brother?
passages.vernacular: 諸神評判我;我冤枉過我嘅敵人嗎?如果不,我點會冤枉一個兄弟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 諸神評判我;我冤枉過我的敵人嗎?如果不,我怎麼會冤枉一個兄弟?

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Brutus, this sober form of yours hides wrongs; And when you do them—
passages.vernacular: 布魯圖斯,你呢莊重嘅外表遮蓋住冤屈;當你做佢哋時——
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布魯圖斯,你這莊重的外表遮蓋著冤屈;當你做它們時——

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Cassius, be content. Speak your griefs softly, I do know you well. Before the eyes of both our armies here, Which should perceive nothing but love from us, Let us not wrangle. Bid them move away; Then in my tent, Cassius, enlarge your griefs, And I will give you audience.
passages.vernacular: 卡修斯,放心。輕聲講你嘅不滿,我好了解你。喺我哋兩軍嘅眼前,佢哋應當從我哋身上睇唔到任何嘢除咗愛,讓我哋唔好爭吵。叫佢哋走開;然後喺我嘅帳篷裡,卡修斯,盡情講你嘅不滿,我會聽你講。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卡修斯,放心。輕聲說你的不滿,我很了解你。在我們兩軍的眼前,他們應當從我們身上看不到任何東西除了愛,讓我們不要爭吵。叫他們走開;然後在我的帳篷裡,卡修斯,盡情說你的不滿,我會聽你說。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Pindarus, Bid our commanders lead their charges off A little from this ground.
passages.vernacular: 平達魯斯,叫我哋嘅指揮官把佢哋嘅部隊從呢片地方帶開啲。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 平達魯斯,叫我們的指揮官把他們的部隊從這片地方帶開一點。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Lucilius, do you the like; and let no man Come to our tent till we have done our conference. Lucius and Titinius, guard our door.
passages.vernacular: 魯西留斯,你都咁樣做;冇人可以到我哋嘅帳篷,直到我哋談完。路修斯同提提紐斯,守喺我哋嘅門口。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 魯西留斯,你也這樣做;沒有人可以到我們的帳篷,直到我們談完。路修斯和提提紐斯,守在我們的門口。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act IV, Scene III — Within the Tent of Brutus 第四幕第三場:布魯圖斯營帳內

passages.original: Enter Brutus and Cassius.
passages.vernacular: [布魯圖斯同卡修斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [布魯圖斯與卡修斯上。]

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: That you have wrong’d me doth appear in this: You have condemn’d and noted Lucius Pella For taking bribes here of the Sardians; Wherein my letters, praying on his side Because I knew the man, were slighted off.
passages.vernacular: 你冤枉我,喺呢件事上好明顯:你譴責並記下盧修斯·佩拉,因為佢喺呢度收受薩迪斯人嘅賄賂;對此我嘅信,為佢講情,因為我認識呢個人,被你輕視。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你冤枉我,在這件事上很明顯:你譴責並記下盧修斯·佩拉,因為他在這裡收受薩迪斯人的賄賂;對此我的信,為他說情,因為我認識這個人,被你輕視。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: You wrong’d yourself to write in such a case.
passages.vernacular: 你為呢種事寫信,係委屈你自己。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為這種事寫信,是委屈你自己。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: In such a time as this it is not meet That every nice offence should bear his comment.
passages.vernacular: 喺咁樣嘅時候,不宜每一樁細小嘅過失都要受評論。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這樣的時候,不宜每一樁細小的過失都要受評論。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Let me tell you, Cassius, you yourself Are much condemn’d to have an itching palm, To sell and mart your offices for gold To undeservers.
passages.vernacular: 讓我告訴你,卡修斯,你自己都大受指責,講你掌心發癢,為金子出賣同買賣你嘅官職畀不配嘅人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 讓我告訴你,卡修斯,你自己也大受指責,說你掌心發癢,為金子出賣和買賣你的官職給不配的人。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: I an itching palm! You know that you are Brutus that speak this, Or, by the gods, this speech were else your last.
passages.vernacular: 我掌心發癢!你知道講呢話嘅係布魯圖斯,否則,憑諸神,呢話就係你最後一句。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我掌心發癢!你知道說這話的是布魯圖斯,否則,憑諸神,這話就是你最後一句。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: The name of Cassius honours this corruption, And chastisement doth therefore hide his head.
passages.vernacular: 卡修斯嘅名字為呢腐敗增光,所以懲罰就躲起嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卡修斯的名字為這腐敗增光,所以懲罰就躲起來。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Chastisement!
passages.vernacular: 懲罰!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 懲罰!

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Remember March, the Ides of March remember: Did not great Julius bleed for justice’ sake? What villain touch’d his body, that did stab, And not for justice? What! Shall one of us, That struck the foremost man of all this world But for supporting robbers, shall we now Contaminate our fingers with base bribes, And sell the mighty space of our large honours For so much trash as may be grasped thus? I had rather be a dog, and bay the moon, Than such a Roman.
passages.vernacular: 記住三月,記住三月十五日:偉大嘅尤利烏斯唔係為了正義而流血嗎?邊個惡棍碰咗佢嘅身體,刺咗佢,唔係為了正義?乜嘢!我哋中嘅一個,刺咗呢世界上最首要嘅人,僅僅因為佢縱容強盜,我哋而家要用卑鄙嘅賄賂玷污我哋嘅手指,把我哋廣大榮譽嘅巨大空間賣掉,換咁樣一把可以握住嘅垃圾嗎?我寧可做一條狗,對月亮吠,都不做咁樣嘅羅馬人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 記住三月,記住三月十五日:偉大的尤利烏斯不是為了正義而流血嗎?哪個惡棍碰了他的身體,刺了他,不是為了正義?什麼!我們中的一個,刺了這世界上最首要的人,僅僅因為他縱容強盜,我們現在要用卑鄙的賄賂玷污我們的手指,把我們廣大榮譽的巨大空間賣掉,換這樣一把可以握住的垃圾嗎?我寧可做一條狗,對月亮吠,也不做這樣的羅馬人。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Brutus, bait not me, I’ll not endure it. You forget yourself, To hedge me in. I am a soldier, I, Older in practice, abler than yourself To make conditions.
passages.vernacular: 布魯圖斯,別逗我,我唔能夠忍受。你忘咗自己,嚟圈住我。我係個軍人,我,經驗比你老,比你更有能力訂立條件。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布魯圖斯,別逗我,我不能忍受。你忘了自己,來圈住我。我是個軍人,我,經驗比你老,比你更有能力訂立條件。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Go to; you are not, Cassius.
passages.vernacular: 算咗吧;你唔係,卡修斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 算了吧;你不是,卡修斯。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: I am.
passages.vernacular: 我係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我是。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: I say you are not.
passages.vernacular: 我講你唔係。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說你不是。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Urge me no more, I shall forget myself; Have mind upon your health, tempt me no farther.
passages.vernacular: 唔好再逼我,我會忘記自己;顧念你嘅健康,唔好再試探我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別再逼我,我會忘記自己;顧念你的健康,別再試探我。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Away, slight man!
passages.vernacular: 走開,卑微嘅人!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走開,卑微的人!

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Is’t possible?
passages.vernacular: 可能嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可能嗎?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Hear me, for I will speak. Must I give way and room to your rash choler? Shall I be frighted when a madman stares?
passages.vernacular: 聽我講,因為我要講話。我要讓位讓路畀你魯莽嘅脾氣嗎?一個瘋子瞪眼,我就要害怕嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽我說,因為我要說話。我要讓位讓路給你魯莽的脾氣嗎?一個瘋子瞪眼,我就要害怕嗎?

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: O ye gods, ye gods! Must I endure all this?
passages.vernacular: 啊諸神,諸神!我必須忍受呢一切嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊諸神,諸神!我必須忍受這一切嗎?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: All this? ay, more: fret till your proud heart break; Go show your slaves how choleric you are, And make your bondmen tremble. Must I budge? Must I observe you? Must I stand and crouch Under your testy humour? By the gods, You shall digest the venom of your spleen, Though it do split you; for, from this day forth, I’ll use you for my mirth, yea, for my laughter, When you are waspish.
passages.vernacular: 呢一切?對,仲有更多:你盡管憤怒,直到你驕傲嘅心碎裂;去向你嘅奴隸顯示你幾咁易怒,使你嘅奴僕發抖。我必須讓步嗎?我必須遷就你嗎?我必須站住屈身喺你暴躁嘅脾氣下嗎?憑諸神,你要消化你怒氣嘅毒液,即使佢撐裂你;因為,從今日起,我要把你當作我嘅笑料,對,我嘅笑話,當你發怒像黃蜂嘅時候。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這一切?對,還有更多:你盡管憤怒,直到你驕傲的心碎裂;去向你的奴隸顯示你多麼易怒,使你的奴僕發抖。我必須讓步嗎?我必須遷就你嗎?我必須站著屈身在你暴躁的脾氣下嗎?憑諸神,你要消化你怒氣的毒液,即使它撐裂你;因為,從今天起,我要把你當作我的笑料,對,我的笑話,當你發怒像黃蜂的時候。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Is it come to this?
passages.vernacular: 竟到咗呢一步嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 竟到了這一步嗎?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: You say you are a better soldier: Let it appear so; make your vaunting true, And it shall please me well. For mine own part, I shall be glad to learn of noble men.
passages.vernacular: 你講你係更好嘅軍人:讓佢顯出嚟吧;讓你嘅誇口成真,我會好高興。就我自己而言,我樂於向高貴嘅人學習。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你說你是更好的軍人:讓它顯出來吧;讓你的誇口成真,我會很高興。就我自己而言,我樂於向高貴的人學習。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: You wrong me every way, you wrong me, Brutus. I said, an elder soldier, not a better: Did I say better?
passages.vernacular: 你各方面都冤枉我,你冤枉我,布魯圖斯。我講嘅係年長嘅軍人,唔係更好嘅:我講更好咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你各方面都冤枉我,你冤枉我,布魯圖斯。我說的是年長的軍人,不是更好的:我說更好了嗎?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: If you did, I care not.
passages.vernacular: 如果你講喇,我不在乎。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果你說了,我不在乎。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: When Caesar liv’d, he durst not thus have mov’d me.
passages.vernacular: 凱撒活住時,佢都唔敢咁樣激怒我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱撒活著時,他也不敢這樣激怒我。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Peace, peace! you durst not so have tempted him.
passages.vernacular: 安靜,安靜!你唔敢咁樣試探佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安靜,安靜!你不敢這樣試探他。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: I durst not?
passages.vernacular: 我唔敢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不敢?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: No.
passages.vernacular: 不。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: What? durst not tempt him?
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢?唔敢試探佢?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼?不敢試探他?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: For your life you durst not.
passages.vernacular: 就算為了你嘅命,你都唔敢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就算為了你的命,你也不敢。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Do not presume too much upon my love. I may do that I shall be sorry for.
passages.vernacular: 別過分依賴我嘅愛。我可能做出我會後悔嘅事。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別過分依賴我的愛。我可能做出我會後悔的事。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: You have done that you should be sorry for. There is no terror, Cassius, in your threats, For I am arm’d so strong in honesty, That they pass by me as the idle wind, Which I respect not. I did send to you For certain sums of gold, which you denied me; For I can raise no money by vile means: By Heaven, I had rather coin my heart, And drop my blood for drachmas, than to wring From the hard hands of peasants their vile trash By any indirection. I did send To you for gold to pay my legions, Which you denied me: was that done like Cassius? Should I have answer’d Caius Cassius so? When Marcus Brutus grows so covetous, To lock such rascal counters from his friends, Be ready, gods, with all your thunderbolts, Dash him to pieces!
passages.vernacular: 你已經做咗你該後悔嘅事。你嘅威脅冇任何恐怖,卡修斯,因為我以誠實武裝得咁強,佢哋像閒風一樣從我身邊吹過,我不予理會。我曾派人向你要一定數量嘅金子,你拒絕咗我;因為我唔能夠用卑劣手段籌款:憑上天,我寧可鑄造我嘅心,為德拉克馬滴下我嘅血,都唔願從農民粗糙嘅手上以任何拐彎抹角嘅方式榨取佢哋卑賤嘅垃圾。我派人向你要金子付我嘅軍團,你拒絕咗我:呢個係卡修斯該做嘅事嗎?我該咁樣答覆凱烏斯·卡修斯嗎?當馬庫斯·布魯圖斯變得咁貪婪,把呢種無賴嘅籌碼鎖住不畀朋友,諸神啊,請準備好你哋所有嘅雷電,把佢打得粉碎!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你已經做了你該後悔的事。你的威脅沒有任何恐怖,卡修斯,因為我以誠實武裝得這麼強,它們像閒風一樣從我身邊吹過,我不予理會。我曾派人向你要一定數量的金子,你拒絕了我;因為我不能用卑劣手段籌款:憑上天,我寧可鑄造我的心,為德拉克馬滴下我的血,也不願從農民粗糙的手上以任何拐彎抹角的方式榨取他們卑賤的垃圾。我派人向你要金子付我的軍團,你拒絕了我:這是卡修斯該做的事嗎?我該這樣答覆凱烏斯·卡修斯嗎?當馬庫斯·布魯圖斯變得這麼貪婪,把這種無賴的籌碼鎖住不給朋友,諸神啊,請準備好你們所有的雷電,把他打得粉碎!

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: I denied you not.
passages.vernacular: 我冇拒絕你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有拒絕你。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: You did.
passages.vernacular: 你有。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你有。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: I did not. He was but a fool That brought my answer back. Brutus hath riv’d my heart. A friend should bear his friend’s infirmities; But Brutus makes mine greater than they are.
passages.vernacular: 我冇。帶我嘅回答回去嘅嗰個人不過係個傻瓜。布魯圖斯撕裂咗我嘅心。朋友應該忍受朋友嘅弱點;但布魯圖斯把我嘅弱點弄得比佢哋本來更大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有。帶我的回答回去的那個人不過是個傻瓜。布魯圖斯撕裂了我的心。朋友應該忍受朋友的弱點;但布魯圖斯把我的弱點弄得比它們本來更大。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: I do not, till you practise them on me.
passages.vernacular: 我冇,直到你把佢哋用喺我身上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒有,直到你把它們用在我身上。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: You love me not.
passages.vernacular: 你不愛我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你不愛我。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: I do not like your faults.
passages.vernacular: 我不鍾意你嘅過失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不喜歡你的過失。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: A friendly eye could never see such faults.
passages.vernacular: 友善嘅眼睛永遠睇唔到咁樣嘅過失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 友善的眼睛永遠看不到這樣的過失。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: A flatterer’s would not, though they do appear As huge as high Olympus.
passages.vernacular: 奉承者嘅眼睛唔會,即使佢哋睇起嚟像高高嘅奧林帕斯山嗰樣巨大。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奉承者的眼睛不會,即使它們看起來像高高的奧林帕斯山那樣巨大。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Come, Antony, and young Octavius, come, Revenge yourselves alone on Cassius, For Cassius is a-weary of the world: Hated by one he loves; brav’d by his brother; Check’d like a bondman; all his faults observ’d, Set in a note-book, learn’d and conn’d by rote, To cast into my teeth. O, I could weep My spirit from mine eyes! There is my dagger, And here my naked breast; within, a heart Dearer than Plutus’ mine, richer than gold: If that thou be’st a Roman, take it forth. I, that denied thee gold, will give my heart: Strike as thou didst at Caesar; for I know, When thou didst hate him worst, thou lovedst him better Than ever thou lovedst Cassius.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,安東尼,同年輕嘅屋大維,嚟,只向卡修斯報仇吧,因為卡修斯厭倦咗世界:被佢所愛嘅人恨;被佢嘅兄弟挑戰;像奴隸一樣被責備;佢所有嘅過失都被觀察、記喺筆記本裡、背熟,用嚟丟到我臉上。啊,我可以把我嘅靈魂從眼睛裡哭出嚟!呢個係我嘅匕首,呢個係我赤裸嘅胸膛;裡面係一顆心,比普路托斯嘅礦更珍貴,比金子更富有:如果你係羅馬人,把佢取出嚟。我,拒絕咗你金子嘅人,將畀你我嘅心:刺吧,像你刺凱撒嗰樣;因為我知道,當你最恨佢嘅時候,你愛佢比你曾愛卡修斯更深。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,安東尼,和年輕的屋大維,來,只向卡修斯報仇吧,因為卡修斯厭倦了世界:被他所愛的人恨;被他的兄弟挑戰;像奴隸一樣被責備;他所有的過失都被觀察、記在筆記本裡、背熟,用來丟到我臉上。啊,我可以把我的靈魂從眼睛裡哭出來!這是我的匕首,這是我赤裸的胸膛;裡面是一顆心,比普路托斯的礦更珍貴,比金子更富有:如果你是羅馬人,把它取出來。我,拒絕了你金子的人,將給你我的心:刺吧,像你刺凱撒那樣;因為我知道,當你最恨他的時候,你愛他比你曾愛卡修斯更深。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Sheathe your dagger. Be angry when you will, it shall have scope; Do what you will, dishonour shall be humour. O Cassius, you are yoked with a lamb That carries anger as the flint bears fire, Who, much enforced, shows a hasty spark, And straight is cold again.
passages.vernacular: 收起你嘅匕首。你想生氣時就生氣吧,佢有佢嘅餘地;你想做乜嘢就做,侮辱都將算作一時嘅脾氣。啊卡修斯,你配嘅係一隻羔羊,佢嘅怒氣像燧石帶火,受強烈逼迫才閃出急促嘅火花,隨即又冷下嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 收起你的匕首。你想生氣時就生氣吧,它有它的餘地;你想做什麼就做,侮辱也將算作一時的脾氣。啊卡修斯,你配的是一隻羔羊,他的怒氣像燧石帶火,受強烈逼迫才閃出急促的火花,隨即又冷下來。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Hath Cassius liv’d To be but mirth and laughter to his Brutus, When grief and blood ill-temper’d vexeth him?
passages.vernacular: 卡修斯活住,就係為了成為佢嘅布魯圖斯嘅笑料,當悲傷同失調嘅血氣困擾佢時?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 卡修斯活著,就是為了成為他的布魯圖斯的笑料,當悲傷和失調的血氣困擾他時?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: When I spoke that, I was ill-temper’d too.
passages.vernacular: 我講嗰話時,我嘅脾氣都不好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我說那話時,我的脾氣也不好。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Do you confess so much? Give me your hand.
passages.vernacular: 你承認咁多?把你嘅手畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你承認這麼多?把你的手給我。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: And my heart too.
passages.vernacular: 仲有我嘅心。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有我的心。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: O Brutus!
passages.vernacular: 啊布魯圖斯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊布魯圖斯!

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: What’s the matter?
passages.vernacular: 點喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了?

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Have not you love enough to bear with me, When that rash humour which my mother gave me Makes me forgetful?
passages.vernacular: 難道你冇足夠嘅愛包容我,當我母親畀我嘅嗰種魯莽脾氣使我忘形?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 難道你沒有足夠的愛包容我,當我母親給我的那種魯莽脾氣使我忘形?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Yes, Cassius; and from henceforth, When you are over-earnest with your Brutus, He’ll think your mother chides, and leave you so.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,卡修斯;從今以後,當你對你嘅布魯圖斯過分認真時,佢會想嗰個係你母親喺責罵,就由你去。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,卡修斯;從今以後,當你對你的布魯圖斯過分認真時,他會想那是你母親在責罵,就由你去。

passages.original: Enter Poet, followed by Lucilius, Titinius and Lucius.
passages.vernacular: [詩人上,魯西留斯、提提紐斯同路修斯跟隨。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [詩人上,魯西留斯、提提紐斯與路修斯跟隨。]

passages.title: Poet 詩人
passages.original: [Within.] Let me go in to see the generals, There is some grudge between ’em; ’tis not meet They be alone.
passages.vernacular: [在內。]讓我進去見將軍哋,佢哋之間有些怨恨;佢哋獨處不合適。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [在內。]讓我進去見將軍們,他們之間有些怨恨;他們獨處不合適。

passages.title: Lucilius 魯西留斯
passages.original: [Within.] You shall not come to them.
passages.vernacular: [在內。]你唔能夠到佢哋嗰度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [在內。]你不能到他們那裡。

passages.title: Poet 詩人
passages.original: [Within.] Nothing but death shall stay me.
passages.vernacular: [在內。]除咗死亡,冇乜嘢能阻止我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: [在內。]除了死亡,沒有什麼能阻止我。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: How now! What’s the matter?
passages.vernacular: 點喇!乜嘢事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 怎麼了!什麼事?

passages.title: Poet 詩人
passages.original: For shame, you generals! What do you mean? Love, and be friends, as two such men should be; For I have seen more years, I’m sure, than ye.
passages.vernacular: 真丟臉,你哋將軍!你哋係乜嘢意思?愛,做朋友,像兩個咁樣嘅人該做嘅;因為我比你哋睇過更多年歲,我確信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 真丟臉,你們將軍!你們是什麼意思?愛,做朋友,像兩個這樣的人該做的;因為我比你們看過更多年歲,我確信。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Ha, ha! How vilely doth this cynic rhyme!
passages.vernacular: 哈,哈!呢個犬儒嘅詩押得幾咁差!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈,哈!這個犬儒的詩押得多麼差!

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Get you hence, sirrah. Saucy fellow, hence!
passages.vernacular: 滾開,小子。無禮嘅傢伙,滾!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 滾開,小子。無禮的傢伙,滾!

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Bear with him, Brutus; ’tis his fashion.
passages.vernacular: 包容佢,布魯圖斯;呢個係佢嘅樣子。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 包容他,布魯圖斯;這是他的樣子。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: I’ll know his humour when he knows his time. What should the wars do with these jigging fools? Companion, hence!
passages.vernacular: 等佢懂得時機,我就懂得佢嘅脾氣。戰爭跟呢啲蹦蹦跳跳嘅傻瓜有乜嘢關係?同伴,走開!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 等他懂得時機,我就懂得他的脾氣。戰爭跟這些蹦蹦跳跳的傻瓜有什麼關係?同伴,走開!

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Away, away, be gone!
passages.vernacular: 走,走,滾!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 走,走,滾!

passages.original: [Exit Poet.]
passages.vernacular: [詩人下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [詩人下。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Lucilius and Titinius, bid the commanders Prepare to lodge their companies tonight.
passages.vernacular: 魯西留斯同提提紐斯,叫指揮官哋準備今晚安排佢哋嘅部隊住宿。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 魯西留斯和提提紐斯,叫指揮官們準備今晚安排他們的部隊住宿。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: And come yourselves and bring Messala with you Immediately to us.
passages.vernacular: 你哋自己都嚟,帶梅薩拉即刻到我哋呢度。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你們自己也來,帶梅薩拉立刻到我們這裡。

passages.original: [Exeunt Lucilius and Titinius.]
passages.vernacular: [魯西留斯同提提紐斯下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [魯西留斯與提提紐斯下。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Lucius, a bowl of wine.
passages.vernacular: 路修斯,一碗酒。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 路修斯,一碗酒。

passages.original: [Exit Lucius.]
passages.vernacular: [路修斯下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [路修斯下。]

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: I did not think you could have been so angry.
passages.vernacular: 我冇想到你會咁生氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我沒想到你會這麼生氣。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: O Cassius, I am sick of many griefs.
passages.vernacular: 啊卡修斯,我為許多悲痛而病。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊卡修斯,我為許多悲痛而病。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Of your philosophy you make no use, If you give place to accidental evils.
passages.vernacular: 你若向偶然嘅邪惡讓步,你嘅哲學就冇用。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你若向偶然的邪惡讓步,你的哲學就沒有用。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: No man bears sorrow better. Portia is dead.
passages.vernacular: 冇人比佢更好地承受悲傷。波西亞死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有人比他更好地承受悲傷。波西亞死了。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Ha? Portia?
passages.vernacular: 哈?波西亞?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哈?波西亞?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: She is dead.
passages.vernacular: 佢死喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 她死了。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: How ’scap’d I killing, when I cross’d you so? O insupportable and touching loss! Upon what sickness?
passages.vernacular: 我咁樣頂撞你,點冇被殺死?啊,難以承受而痛心嘅損失!因乜嘢病?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我這樣頂撞你,怎麼沒被殺死?啊,難以承受而痛心的損失!因什麼病?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Impatient of my absence, And grief that young Octavius with Mark Antony Have made themselves so strong; for with her death That tidings came. With this she fell distract, And, her attendants absent, swallow’d fire.
passages.vernacular: 因為忍受不了我不喺,並為年輕嘅屋大維同馬克·安東尼變得如此強大而悲傷;因為隨佢嘅死傳嚟咗嗰個消息。因此佢發瘋,侍從不喺時,吞下咗火。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 因為忍受不了我不在,並為年輕的屋大維與馬克·安東尼變得如此強大而悲傷;因為隨她的死傳來了那個消息。因此她發瘋,侍從不在時,吞下了火。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: And died so?
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣死喇?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣死了?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Even so.
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: O ye immortal gods!
passages.vernacular: 啊不朽嘅諸神!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊不朽的諸神!

passages.original: Enter Lucius, with wine and a taper.
passages.vernacular: [路修斯端酒同蠟燭上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [路修斯端酒與蠟燭上。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Speak no more of her. Give me a bowl of wine. In this I bury all unkindness, Cassius.
passages.vernacular: 唔好再提佢。畀我一碗酒。我喺此埋葬一切不友善,卡修斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別再提她。給我一碗酒。我在此埋葬一切不友善,卡修斯。

passages.original: [Drinks.]

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: My heart is thirsty for that noble pledge. Fill, Lucius, till the wine o’erswell the cup. I cannot drink too much of Brutus’ love.
passages.vernacular: 我嘅心渴望嗰高貴嘅祝酒。斟吧,路修斯,直到酒漫過杯子。我飲唔夠布魯圖斯嘅愛。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我的心渴望那高貴的祝酒。斟吧,路修斯,直到酒漫過杯子。我喝不夠布魯圖斯的愛。

passages.original: [Drinks.]
[Exit Lucius.]
passages.vernacular: [路修斯下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [路修斯下。]

passages.original: Enter Titinius and Messala.
passages.vernacular: [提提紐斯同梅薩拉上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [提提紐斯與梅薩拉上。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Come in, Titinius! Welcome, good Messala. Now sit we close about this taper here, And call in question our necessities.
passages.vernacular: 進嚟,提提紐斯!歡迎,好梅薩拉。而家讓我哋緊靠呢支蠟燭坐,討論我哋嘅急務。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 進來,提提紐斯!歡迎,好梅薩拉。現在讓我們緊靠這支蠟燭坐,討論我們的急務。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Portia, art thou gone?
passages.vernacular: 波西亞,你走咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 波西亞,你走了嗎?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: No more, I pray you. Messala, I have here received letters, That young Octavius and Mark Antony Come down upon us with a mighty power, Bending their expedition toward Philippi.
passages.vernacular: 唔好再講喇,求你。梅薩拉,我呢度收到信,講年輕嘅屋大維同馬克·安東尼帶住強大嘅兵力向我哋逼近,朝腓力比進軍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 別再說了,求你。梅薩拉,我這裡收到信,說年輕的屋大維和馬克·安東尼帶著強大的兵力向我們逼近,朝腓力比進軍。

passages.title: Messala 梅薩拉
passages.original: Myself have letters of the selfsame tenor.
passages.vernacular: 我自己都有同樣內容嘅信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我自己也有同樣內容的信。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: With what addition?
passages.vernacular: 仲有乜嘢附加嘅?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還有什麼附加的?

passages.title: Messala 梅薩拉
passages.original: That by proscription and bills of outlawry Octavius, Antony, and Lepidus Have put to death an hundred Senators.
passages.vernacular: 講屋大維、安東尼同雷必達用放逐令同褫奪公權嘅文告處死咗一百個元老。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 說屋大維、安東尼和雷必達用放逐令和褫奪公權的文告處死了一百個元老。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Therein our letters do not well agree. Mine speak of seventy Senators that died By their proscriptions, Cicero being one.
passages.vernacular: 喺呢點上我哋嘅信不太一致。我嘅信講七十個元老死於佢哋嘅放逐令,西塞羅係其中之一。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在這點上我們的信不太一致。我的信說七十個元老死於他們的放逐令,西塞羅是其中之一。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Cicero one!
passages.vernacular: 西塞羅係其中之一!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 西塞羅是其中之一!

passages.title: Messala 梅薩拉
passages.original: Cicero is dead, And by that order of proscription. Had you your letters from your wife, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 西塞羅死喇,就死喺嗰道放逐令下。大人,您收到妻子嘅信嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 西塞羅死了,就死在那道放逐令下。大人,您收到妻子的信嗎?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: No, Messala.
passages.vernacular: 冇,梅薩拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,梅薩拉。

passages.title: Messala 梅薩拉
passages.original: Nor nothing in your letters writ of her?
passages.vernacular: 您嘅信裡都冇寫到佢任何事?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 您的信裡也沒寫到她任何事?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Nothing, Messala.
passages.vernacular: 冇,梅薩拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,梅薩拉。

passages.title: Messala 梅薩拉
passages.original: That, methinks, is strange.
passages.vernacular: 我覺得呢個好奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我覺得這很奇怪。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Why ask you? Hear you aught of her in yours?
passages.vernacular: 你點解問?你聽到你嗰邊有關於佢嘅消息嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼問?你聽到你那邊有關於她的消息嗎?

passages.title: Messala 梅薩拉
passages.original: No, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 冇,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,大人。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Now as you are a Roman, tell me true.
passages.vernacular: 既然你係羅馬人,就告訴我真話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 既然你是羅馬人,就告訴我真話。

passages.title: Messala 梅薩拉
passages.original: Then like a Roman bear the truth I tell, For certain she is dead, and by strange manner.
passages.vernacular: 咁就像羅馬人一樣承受我講嘅真話,佢肯定係死喇,而且死得好奇怪。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼就像羅馬人一樣承受我說的真話,她肯定是死了,而且死得很奇怪。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Why, farewell, Portia. We must die, Messala. With meditating that she must die once, I have the patience to endure it now.
passages.vernacular: 哎,再會,波西亞。我哋都必須死,梅薩拉。因為想到佢終有一死,我而家有耐心忍受佢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 哎,再會,波西亞。我們都必須死,梅薩拉。因為想到她終有一死,我現在有耐心忍受它。

passages.title: Messala 梅薩拉
passages.original: Even so great men great losses should endure.
passages.vernacular: 偉人就係咁樣承受大嘅損失。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 偉人就是這樣承受大的損失。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: I have as much of this in art as you, But yet my nature could not bear it so.
passages.vernacular: 喺理論上我同你一樣懂呢個,但我嘅天性卻唔能夠咁樣承受。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在理論上我與你一樣懂這個,但我的天性卻不能這樣承受。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Well, to our work alive. What do you think Of marching to Philippi presently?
passages.vernacular: 好,回到我哋活人嘅工作。你認為即刻向腓力比進軍如何?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,回到我們活人的工作。你認為立刻向腓力比進軍如何?

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: I do not think it good.
passages.vernacular: 我認為不好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我認為不好。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Your reason?
passages.vernacular: 你嘅理由?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的理由?

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: This it is: ’Tis better that the enemy seek us; So shall he waste his means, weary his soldiers, Doing himself offence, whilst we, lying still, Are full of rest, defence, and nimbleness.
passages.vernacular: 係咁樣:敵人嚟找我哋更好;咁樣佢會耗費佢嘅資源,疲勞佢嘅士兵,自己損害自己,而我哋靜止不動,充滿休息、防守同敏捷。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是這樣:敵人來找我們更好;這樣他會耗費他的資源,疲勞他的士兵,自己損害自己,而我們靜止不動,充滿休息、防守和敏捷。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Good reasons must of force give place to better. The people ’twixt Philippi and this ground Do stand but in a forced affection; For they have grudg’d us contribution. The enemy, marching along by them, By them shall make a fuller number up, Come on refresh’d, new-added, and encourag’d; From which advantage shall we cut him off If at Philippi we do face him there, These people at our back.
passages.vernacular: 好嘅理由必須讓位畀更好嘅。腓力比同呢片地之間嘅人民只係被迫地擁護我哋;因為佢哋對畀我哋納貢好不情願。敵人從佢哋身邊經過,將從佢哋嗰度補足人數,嚟時精神煥發、新添兵員、受到鼓舞;如果我哋喺腓力比同佢對陣,呢啲人民喺我哋背後,我哋就切不斷佢呢啲優勢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好的理由必須讓位給更好的。腓力比與這片地之間的人民只是被迫地擁護我們;因為他們對給我們納貢很不情願。敵人從他們身邊經過,將從他們那裡補足人數,來時精神煥發、新添兵員、受到鼓舞;如果我們在腓力比與他對陣,這些人民在我們背後,我們就切不斷他這些優勢。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Hear me, good brother.
passages.vernacular: 聽我講,好兄弟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 聽我說,好兄弟。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Under your pardon. You must note besides, That we have tried the utmost of our friends, Our legions are brim-full, our cause is ripe. The enemy increaseth every day; We, at the height, are ready to decline. There is a tide in the affairs of men, Which, taken at the flood, leads on to fortune; Omitted, all the voyage of their life Is bound in shallows and in miseries. On such a full sea are we now afloat, And we must take the current when it serves, Or lose our ventures.
passages.vernacular: 恕我打斷。你仲要注意,我哋已把朋友嘅力量用盡,我哋嘅軍團滿滿嘅,我哋嘅事業成熟。敵人每天增加;我哋已到頂點,準備衰落。人事有潮水,趁漲潮抓住佢,便通向幸運;錯過喇,一生嘅整個航程都困喺淺灘同悲慘中。我哋而家就漂浮喺咁樣嘅滿潮上,必須趁水流順時順流而行,否則會失去我哋嘅冒險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 恕我打斷。你還要注意,我們已把朋友的力量用盡,我們的軍團滿滿的,我們的事業成熟。敵人每天增加;我們已到頂點,準備衰落。人事有潮水,趁漲潮抓住它,便通向幸運;錯過了,一生的整個航程都困在淺灘和悲慘中。我們現在就漂浮在這樣的滿潮上,必須趁水流順時順流而行,否則會失去我們的冒險。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Then, with your will, go on: We’ll along ourselves, and meet them at Philippi.
passages.vernacular: 咁,隨你嘅意願,前進:我哋自己都同去,喺腓力比迎戰佢哋。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,隨你的意願,前進:我們自己也同去,在腓力比迎戰他們。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: The deep of night is crept upon our talk, And nature must obey necessity, Which we will niggard with a little rest. There is no more to say?
passages.vernacular: 深夜已爬上我哋嘅談話,自然必須服從需要,我哋將吝嗇地只畀啲休息。冇別嘅要講咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 深夜已爬上我們的談話,自然必須服從需要,我們將吝嗇地只給一點休息。沒有別的要說了嗎?

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: No more. Good night: Early tomorrow will we rise, and hence.
passages.vernacular: 冇喇。晚安:聽日一早我哋起身離開。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有了。晚安:明天一早我們起身離開。

passages.original: Enter Lucius.
passages.vernacular: [路修斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [路修斯上。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Lucius! My gown.
passages.vernacular: 路修斯!我嘅瞓袍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 路修斯!我的睡袍。

passages.original: [Exit Lucius.]
passages.vernacular: [路修斯下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [路修斯下。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Farewell now, good Messala. Good night, Titinius. Noble, noble Cassius, Good night, and good repose.
passages.vernacular: 而家再會,好梅薩拉。晚安,提提紐斯。高貴嘅、高貴嘅卡修斯,晚安,好好休息。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在再會,好梅薩拉。晚安,提提紐斯。高貴的、高貴的卡修斯,晚安,好好休息。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: O my dear brother! This was an ill beginning of the night. Never come such division ’tween our souls! Let it not, Brutus.
passages.vernacular: 啊我親愛嘅兄弟!呢個係夜晚嘅一個糟糕開頭。但願我哋嘅靈魂之間永唔再有咁樣嘅分裂!唔會嘅,布魯圖斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊我親愛的兄弟!這是夜晚的一個糟糕開頭。但願我們的靈魂之間永不再有這樣的分裂!不會的,布魯圖斯。

passages.original: Enter Lucius with the gown.
passages.vernacular: [路修斯攞住瞓袍上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [路修斯拿著睡袍上。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Everything is well.
passages.vernacular: 一切都好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一切都好。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Good night, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 晚安,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚安,大人。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Good night, good brother.
passages.vernacular: 晚安,好兄弟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚安,好兄弟。

passages.title: Titinius and Messala 提提紐斯與梅薩拉
passages.original: Good night, Lord Brutus.
passages.vernacular: 晚安,布魯圖斯大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 晚安,布魯圖斯大人。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Farewell, everyone.
passages.vernacular: 各位再會。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 各位再會。

passages.original: [Exeunt Cassius, Titinius and Messala.]
passages.vernacular: [卡修斯、提提紐斯同梅薩拉下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [卡修斯、提提紐斯與梅薩拉下。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Give me the gown. Where is thy instrument?
passages.vernacular: 把瞓袍畀我。你嘅樂器喺邊度?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 把睡袍給我。你的樂器在哪裡?

passages.title: Lucius 路修斯
passages.original: Here in the tent.
passages.vernacular: 喺帳篷裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 在帳篷裡。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: What, thou speak’st drowsily? Poor knave, I blame thee not, thou art o’er-watch’d. Call Claudius and some other of my men; I’ll have them sleep on cushions in my tent.
passages.vernacular: 乜嘢,你講話昏昏沉沉嘅?可憐嘅細路,我不怪你,你熬夜過度喇。叫克勞狄烏斯同我另外啲人;我要佢哋瞓喺我帳篷裡嘅墊子上。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 什麼,你說話昏昏沉沉的?可憐的孩子,我不怪你,你熬夜過度了。叫克勞狄烏斯和我另外一些人;我要他們睡在我帳篷裡的墊子上。

passages.title: Lucius 路修斯
passages.original: Varro and Claudius!
passages.vernacular: 瓦羅同克勞狄烏斯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 瓦羅和克勞狄烏斯!

passages.original: Enter Varro and Claudius.
passages.vernacular: [瓦羅同克勞狄烏斯上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [瓦羅與克勞狄烏斯上。]

passages.title: Varro 瓦羅
passages.original: Calls my lord?
passages.vernacular: 大人叫我哋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人叫我們?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: I pray you, sirs, lie in my tent and sleep; It may be I shall raise you by-and-by On business to my brother Cassius.
passages.vernacular: 請你哋,先生哋,瞓喺我帳篷裡;我可能不久會叫醒你哋,去辦件事找我兄弟卡修斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 請你們,先生們,睡在我帳篷裡;我可能不久會叫醒你們,去辦件事找我兄弟卡修斯。

passages.title: Varro 瓦羅
passages.original: So please you, we will stand and watch your pleasure.
passages.vernacular: 如果您願意,我哋就站住等候您嘅吩咐。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 如果您願意,我們就站著等候您的吩咐。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: I will not have it so; lie down, good sirs, It may be I shall otherwise bethink me. Look, Lucius, here’s the book I sought for so; I put it in the pocket of my gown.
passages.vernacular: 我唔好咁樣;躺下,好先生哋,我可能改變主意。睇,路修斯,呢個係我苦苦找嘅書;我把佢放喺我瞓袍嘅口袋裡。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不要這樣;躺下,好先生們,我可能改變主意。看,路修斯,這是我苦苦找的書;我把它放在我睡袍的口袋裡。

passages.original: [Servants lie down.]
passages.vernacular: [僕人哋躺下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [僕人們躺下。]

passages.title: Lucius 路修斯
passages.original: I was sure your lordship did not give it me.
passages.vernacular: 我確定大人冇畀我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我確定大人沒有給我。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Bear with me, good boy, I am much forgetful. Canst thou hold up thy heavy eyes awhile, And touch thy instrument a strain or two?
passages.vernacular: 包容我,好細路,我好健忘。你能撐住你沉重嘅眼睛一會兒,彈一兩曲嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 包容我,好孩子,我很健忘。你能撐著你沉重的眼睛一會兒,彈一兩曲嗎?

passages.title: Lucius 路修斯
passages.original: Ay, my lord, an’t please you.
passages.vernacular: 可以,大人,如果您願意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 可以,大人,如果您願意。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: It does, my boy. I trouble thee too much, but thou art willing.
passages.vernacular: 願意,我嘅細路。我太麻煩你喇,但你好願意。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 願意,我的孩子。我太麻煩你了,但你很願意。

passages.title: Lucius 路修斯
passages.original: It is my duty, sir.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係我嘅職責,先生。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是我的職責,先生。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: I should not urge thy duty past thy might; I know young bloods look for a time of rest.
passages.vernacular: 我不該把你嘅職責逼過你嘅力量;我知道年輕人想要休息嘅時間。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不該把你的職責逼過你的力量;我知道年輕人想要休息的時間。

passages.title: Lucius 路修斯
passages.original: I have slept, my lord, already.
passages.vernacular: 我已經瞓過喇,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我已經睡過了,大人。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: It was well done, and thou shalt sleep again; I will not hold thee long. If I do live, I will be good to thee.
passages.vernacular: 咁樣好好,你仲可以再瞓;我唔會留你太久。如果我活住,我會對你好。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這樣很好,你還可以再睡;我不會留你太久。如果我活著,我會對你好。

passages.original: [Lucius plays and sings till he falls asleep.]
passages.vernacular: [路修斯彈奏歌唱,直到瞓住。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [路修斯彈奏歌唱,直到睡著。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: This is a sleepy tune. O murd’rous slumber, Layest thou thy leaden mace upon my boy, That plays thee music? Gentle knave, good night; I will not do thee so much wrong to wake thee. If thou dost nod, thou break’st thy instrument; I’ll take it from thee; and, good boy, good night. Let me see, let me see; is not the leaf turn’d down Where I left reading? Here it is, I think.
passages.vernacular: 呢個係首催眠曲。啊,謀殺性嘅瞓眠,你把鉛製嘅權杖放喺畀你奏樂嘅我嘅細路身上嗎?溫和嘅細路,晚安;我唔會咁樣冤枉你,把你叫醒。如果你點頭,你會弄壞你嘅樂器;我嚟把佢從你手上攞走;好細路,晚安。讓我睇睇,讓我睇睇;我頭先讀到嘅地方嘅書頁唔係折起嚟嘅嗎?喺呢度,我想。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這是首催眠曲。啊,謀殺性的睡眠,你把鉛製的權杖放在給你奏樂的我的孩子身上嗎?溫和的孩子,晚安;我不會這樣冤枉你,把你叫醒。如果你點頭,你會弄壞你的樂器;我來把它從你手上拿走;好孩子,晚安。讓我看看,讓我看看;我剛才讀到的地方的書頁不是折起來的嗎?在這裡,我想。

passages.original: Enter the Ghost of Caesar.
passages.vernacular: [凱撒嘅鬼魂上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [凱撒的鬼魂上。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: How ill this taper burns! Ha! who comes here? I think it is the weakness of mine eyes That shapes this monstrous apparition. It comes upon me. Art thou anything? Art thou some god, some angel, or some devil, That mak’st my blood cold and my hair to stare? Speak to me what thou art.
passages.vernacular: 呢蠟燭燒得多差!哈!邊個嚟喇?我想係我眼睛嘅虛弱造出咗呢個怪異嘅幻象。佢朝我嚟喇。你係乜嘢嘢嗎?你係乜嘢神、乜嘢天使或乜嘢魔鬼,使我嘅血變冷,頭髮豎立?告訴我你係乜嘢。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 這蠟燭燒得多差!哈!誰來了?我想是我眼睛的虛弱造出了這個怪異的幻象。它朝我來了。你是什麼東西嗎?你是什麼神、什麼天使或什麼魔鬼,使我的血變冷,頭髮豎立?告訴我你是什麼。

passages.title: Ghost 鬼魂
passages.original: Thy evil spirit, Brutus.
passages.vernacular: 你嘅惡靈,布魯圖斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你的惡靈,布魯圖斯。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Why com’st thou?
passages.vernacular: 你點解嚟?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼來?

passages.title: Ghost 鬼魂
passages.original: To tell thee thou shalt see me at Philippi.
passages.vernacular: 嚟告訴你,你將喺腓力比見到我。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來告訴你,你將在腓力比見到我。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Well; then I shall see thee again?
passages.vernacular: 好;咁我仲會再見到你?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好;那麼我還會再見到你?

passages.title: Ghost 鬼魂
passages.original: Ay, at Philippi.
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,喺腓力比。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,在腓力比。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Why, I will see thee at Philippi then.
passages.vernacular: 好,咁我就喺腓力比見你。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好,那麼我就在腓力比見你。

passages.original: [Ghost vanishes.]
passages.vernacular: [鬼魂消失。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [鬼魂消失。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Now I have taken heart, thou vanishest. Ill spirit, I would hold more talk with thee. Boy! Lucius! Varro! Claudius! Sirs, awake! Claudius!
passages.vernacular: 而家我鼓起咗勇氣,你就消失喇。惡靈,我想同你多談。細路!路修斯!瓦羅!克勞狄烏斯!先生哋,醒嚟!克勞狄烏斯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在我鼓起了勇氣,你就消失了。惡靈,我想同你多談。孩子!路修斯!瓦羅!克勞狄烏斯!先生們,醒來!克勞狄烏斯!

passages.title: Lucius 路修斯
passages.original: The strings, my lord, are false.
passages.vernacular: 琴弦,大人,走音喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 琴弦,大人,走音了。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: He thinks he still is at his instrument. Lucius, awake!
passages.vernacular: 佢以為自己仲喺彈樂器。路修斯,醒嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他以為自己還在彈樂器。路修斯,醒來!

passages.title: Lucius 路修斯
passages.original: My lord?
passages.vernacular: 大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Didst thou dream, Lucius, that thou so criedst out?
passages.vernacular: 路修斯,你係唔係做夢,所以咁樣喊叫?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 路修斯,你是不是做夢,所以這樣喊叫?

passages.title: Lucius 路修斯
passages.original: My lord, I do not know that I did cry.
passages.vernacular: 大人,我唔知道我喊喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人,我不知道我喊了。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Yes, that thou didst. Didst thou see anything?
passages.vernacular: 係嘅,你喊喇。你睇見乜嘢咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 是的,你喊了。你看見什麼了嗎?

passages.title: Lucius 路修斯
passages.original: Nothing, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 冇,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,大人。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Sleep again, Lucius. Sirrah Claudius! Fellow thou, awake!
passages.vernacular: 再瞓吧,路修斯。克勞狄烏斯!你呢傢伙,醒嚟!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 再睡吧,路修斯。克勞狄烏斯!你這傢伙,醒來!

passages.title: Varro 瓦羅
passages.original: My lord?
passages.vernacular: 大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人?

passages.title: Claudius 克勞狄烏斯
passages.original: My lord?
passages.vernacular: 大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Why did you so cry out, sirs, in your sleep?
passages.vernacular: 先生哋,你哋瞓夢中點解咁樣喊叫?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先生們,你們睡夢中為什麼這樣喊叫?

passages.title: Varro and Claudius 瓦羅與克勞狄烏斯
passages.original: Did we, my lord?
passages.vernacular: 我哋喊咗嗎,大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我們喊了嗎,大人?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Ay. Saw you anything?
passages.vernacular: 對。你哋睇見乜嘢咗嗎?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 對。你們看見什麼了嗎?

passages.title: Varro 瓦羅
passages.original: No, my lord, I saw nothing.
passages.vernacular: 冇,大人,我乜嘢都冇睇見。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 沒有,大人,我什麼也沒看見。

passages.title: Claudius 克勞狄烏斯
passages.original: Nor I, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 我都冇,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也沒有,大人。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Go and commend me to my brother Cassius; Bid him set on his powers betimes before, And we will follow.
passages.vernacular: 去替我向我兄弟卡修斯致意;叫佢及早派佢嘅兵力先行,我哋跟隨。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 去替我向我兄弟卡修斯致意;叫他及早派他的兵力先行,我們跟隨。

passages.title: Varro and Claudius 瓦羅與克勞狄烏斯
passages.original: It shall be done, my lord.
passages.vernacular: 會辦到嘅,大人。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 會辦到的,大人。

passages.original: [Exeunt.]
passages.vernacular: [同下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [同下。]

chapters.title: Act V, Scene I — The Plains of Philippi 第五幕第一場:腓力比平原

passages.original: Enter Octavius, Antony and their Army.
passages.vernacular: [屋大維、安東尼及其軍隊上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [屋大維、安東尼及其軍隊上。]

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: Now, Antony, our hopes are answered. You said the enemy would not come down, But keep the hills and upper regions. It proves not so; their battles are at hand, They mean to warn us at Philippi here, Answering before we do demand of them.
passages.vernacular: 而家,安東尼,我哋嘅希望實現喇。你講過敵人唔會下嚟,只會守喺山上同高處。事實唔係咁樣;佢哋嘅軍隊已近喺眼前,佢哋打算喺呢度腓力比向我哋挑戰,不等我哋去問佢哋就先嚟回應。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,安東尼,我們的希望實現了。你說過敵人不會下來,只會守在山上和高處。事實不是這樣;他們的軍隊已近在眼前,他們打算在這裡腓力比向我們挑戰,不等我們去問他們就先來回應。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Tut, I am in their bosoms, and I know Wherefore they do it. They could be content To visit other places, and come down With fearful bravery, thinking by this face To fasten in our thoughts that they have courage; But ’tis not so.
passages.vernacular: 嘿,我深知佢哋嘅心思,都知道佢哋點解咁樣做。佢哋本來寧願去別嘅地方,卻帶住可怕嘅氣勢下嚟,以為憑呢副面孔,就能讓我哋心裡認定佢哋有勇氣;但事實唔係咁樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 嘿,我深知他們的心思,也知道他們為什麼這樣做。他們本來寧願去別的地方,卻帶著可怕的氣勢下來,以為憑這副面孔,就能讓我們心裡認定他們有勇氣;但事實不是這樣。

passages.original: Enter a Messenger.
passages.vernacular: [一使者上。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [一使者上。]

passages.title: Messenger 信使
passages.original: Prepare you, generals. The enemy comes on in gallant show; Their bloody sign of battle is hung out, And something to be done immediately.
passages.vernacular: 將軍哋,準備吧。敵人以威武嘅陣勢前進;佢哋血紅嘅作戰旗號已經掛出,必須即刻有所行動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將軍們,準備吧。敵人以威武的陣勢前進;他們血紅的作戰旗號已經掛出,必須立刻有所行動。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Octavius, lead your battle softly on Upon the left hand of the even field.
passages.vernacular: 屋大維,你帶你嘅軍隊慢慢開進平坦戰場嘅左邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 屋大維,你帶你的軍隊慢慢開進平坦戰場的左邊。

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: Upon the right hand I. Keep thou the left.
passages.vernacular: 我喺右邊。你守左邊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我在右邊。你守左邊。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Why do you cross me in this exigent?
passages.vernacular: 你點解喺呢緊要關頭同我作對?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 你為什麼在這緊要關頭同我作對?

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: I do not cross you; but I will do so.
passages.vernacular: 我唔係同你作對;不過我就要咁樣做。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我不是同你作對;不過我就要這樣做。

passages.original: [March.]
passages.vernacular: [行軍。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [行軍。]

passages.original: Drum. Enter Brutus, Cassius and their Army; Lucilius, Titinius, Messala and others.
passages.vernacular: [鼓聲。布魯圖斯、卡修斯及其軍隊上;魯西留斯、提提紐斯、梅薩拉及其他人。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [鼓聲。布魯圖斯、卡修斯及其軍隊上;魯西留斯、提提紐斯、梅薩拉及其他人。]

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: They stand, and would have parley.
passages.vernacular: 佢哋站住喇,想要談判。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 他們站住了,想要談判。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Stand fast, Titinius; we must out and talk.
passages.vernacular: 提提紐斯,站穩;我哋必須出去談話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 提提紐斯,站穩;我們必須出去談話。

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: Mark Antony, shall we give sign of battle?
passages.vernacular: 馬克·安東尼,我哋要唔好發出開戰嘅信號?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 馬克·安東尼,我們要不要發出開戰的信號?

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: No, Caesar, we will answer on their charge. Make forth; the generals would have some words.
passages.vernacular: 不,凱撒,等佢哋進攻我哋再回應。出去吧;將軍哋想講幾句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,凱撒,等他們進攻我們再回應。出去吧;將軍們想說幾句話。

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: Stir not until the signal.
passages.vernacular: 信號發出以前唔好動。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 信號發出以前不要動。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Words before blows: is it so, countrymen?
passages.vernacular: 先講話後動手:係咁樣嗎,同胞哋?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 先說話後動手:是這樣嗎,同胞們?

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: Not that we love words better, as you do.
passages.vernacular: 唔係我哋更愛講話,像你嗰樣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不是我們更愛說話,像你那樣。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Good words are better than bad strokes, Octavius.
passages.vernacular: 屋大維,好話勝過壞嘅攻擊。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 屋大維,好話勝過壞的攻擊。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: In your bad strokes, Brutus, you give good words; Witness the hole you made in Caesar’s heart, Crying, “Long live! Hail, Caesar!”
passages.vernacular: 布魯圖斯,你嘅壞攻擊,同時伴住好話;睇你喺凱撒心上刺出嘅嗰個洞,你哋喊住:「萬歲!凱撒萬歲!」
passages.vernacularMandarin: 布魯圖斯,你的壞攻擊,同時伴著好話;看你在凱撒心上刺出的那個洞,你們喊著:「萬歲!凱撒萬歲!」

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Antony, The posture of your blows are yet unknown; But for your words, they rob the Hybla bees, And leave them honeyless.
passages.vernacular: 安東尼,你嗰啲攻擊嘅姿態我哋仲唔知道;至於你嘅話,佢哋搶光咗希布拉嘅蜜蜂,讓牠哋冇蜜。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 安東尼,你那些攻擊的姿態我們還不知道;至於你的話,它們搶光了希布拉的蜜蜂,讓牠們沒有蜜。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Not stingless too.
passages.vernacular: 都唔係冇刺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 也不是沒有刺。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: O yes, and soundless too, For you have stol’n their buzzing, Antony, And very wisely threat before you sting.
passages.vernacular: 啊,係嘅,而且冇聲音,因為你已偷咗牠哋嘅嗡嗡聲,安東尼,仲好聰明地喺你刺人前先發出威脅。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,是的,而且沒有聲音,因為你已偷了牠們的嗡嗡聲,安東尼,還很聰明地在你刺人前先發出威脅。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Villains, you did not so when your vile daggers Hack’d one another in the sides of Caesar: You show’d your teeth like apes, and fawn’d like hounds, And bow’d like bondmen, kissing Caesar’s feet; Whilst damned Casca, like a cur, behind Struck Caesar on the neck. O you flatterers!
passages.vernacular: 惡棍哋,你哋嘅卑鄙匕首喺凱撒身上互相砍刺嘅時候,你哋可唔係咁樣:你哋像猿猴一樣露出牙齒,像獵犬一樣獻媚,像奴隸一樣鞠躬,親吻凱撒嘅腳;同時該死嘅卡斯卡,像一條野狗,從背後刺中凱撒嘅脖子。啊,你哋呢啲奉承者!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 惡棍們,你們的卑鄙匕首在凱撒身上互相砍刺的時候,你們可不是這樣:你們像猿猴一樣露出牙齒,像獵犬一樣獻媚,像奴隸一樣鞠躬,親吻凱撒的腳;同時該死的卡斯卡,像一條野狗,從背後刺中凱撒的脖子。啊,你們這些奉承者!

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Flatterers! Now, Brutus, thank yourself. This tongue had not offended so today, If Cassius might have rul’d.
passages.vernacular: 奉承者!而家,布魯圖斯,謝你自己吧。今日呢舌頭本來唔會咁樣得罪人,如果卡修斯嘅意見被採納嘅話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 奉承者!現在,布魯圖斯,謝你自己吧。今天這舌頭本來不會這樣得罪人,如果卡修斯的意見被採納的話。

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: Come, come, the cause. If arguing makes us sweat, The proof of it will turn to redder drops. Look, I draw a sword against conspirators. When think you that the sword goes up again? Never, till Caesar’s three and thirty wounds Be well aveng’d; or till another Caesar Have added slaughter to the sword of traitors.
passages.vernacular: 嚟吧,嚟吧,談正事。如果爭辯使我哋出汗,證明嘅結果將係更紅嘅血滴。睇,我拔劍對付陰謀者。你哋認為呢劍乜嘢時候才會收回鞘?永遠唔會,直到凱撒嘅三十三處傷口得到好好報復;或者直到另一個凱撒,為叛徒哋嘅劍增添屠殺。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來吧,來吧,談正事。如果爭辯使我們出汗,證明的結果將是更紅的血滴。看,我拔劍對付陰謀者。你們認為這劍什麼時候才會收回鞘?永遠不會,直到凱撒的三十三處傷口得到好好報復;或者直到另一個凱撒,為叛徒們的劍增添屠殺。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Caesar, thou canst not die by traitors’ hands, Unless thou bring’st them with thee.
passages.vernacular: 凱撒,你唔會死喺叛徒嘅手上,除非你自己把佢哋帶嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 凱撒,你不會死在叛徒的手上,除非你自己把他們帶來。

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: So I hope. I was not born to die on Brutus’ sword.
passages.vernacular: 我都咁樣希望。我生來唔係要死喺布魯圖斯嘅劍下。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也這樣希望。我生來不是要死在布魯圖斯的劍下。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: O, if thou wert the noblest of thy strain, Young man, thou couldst not die more honourable.
passages.vernacular: 啊,年輕人,即使你係你家族中最高貴嘅人,你都唔可能死得更光榮。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 啊,年輕人,即使你是你家族中最高貴的人,你也不可能死得更光榮。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: A peevish school-boy, worthless of such honour, Join’d with a masker and a reveller.
passages.vernacular: 一個任性嘅學童,不配得咁樣嘅榮譽,同一個戴面具嘅人同一個尋歡作樂嘅人為伍。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 一個任性的學童,不配得這樣的榮譽,同一個戴面具的人和一個尋歡作樂的人為伍。

passages.title: Antony 安東尼
passages.original: Old Cassius still!
passages.vernacular: 定係老樣子嘅卡修斯!
passages.vernacularMandarin: 還是老樣子的卡修斯!

passages.title: Octavius 屋大維
passages.original: Come, Antony; away! Defiance, traitors, hurl we in your teeth. If you dare fight today, come to the field; If not, when you have stomachs.
passages.vernacular: 嚟,安東尼;走吧!叛徒哋,我哋向你哋臉上扔下挑戰。如果你哋今日敢打,就到戰場上嚟;如果唔敢,等你哋有膽量嘅時候再嚟。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 來,安東尼;走吧!叛徒們,我們向你們臉上扔下挑戰。如果你們今天敢打,就到戰場上來;如果不敢,等你們有膽量的時候再來。

passages.original: [Exeunt Octavius, Antony and their Army.]
passages.vernacular: [屋大維、安東尼及其軍隊下。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [屋大維、安東尼及其軍隊下。]

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Why now, blow wind, swell billow, and swim bark! The storm is up, and all is on the hazard.
passages.vernacular: 好喇,而家,吹吧風,漲吧浪,漂吧船!風暴已起,一切都喺賭一把。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 好了,現在,吹吧風,漲吧浪,漂吧船!風暴已起,一切都在賭一把。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Ho, Lucilius! Hark, a word with you.
passages.vernacular: 喂,魯西留斯!聽住,我同你講句話。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 喂,魯西留斯!聽著,我同你說句話。

passages.title: Lucilius 魯西留斯
passages.original: My lord?
passages.vernacular: 大人?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 大人?

passages.original: [Brutus and Lucilius talk apart.]
passages.vernacular: [布魯圖斯同魯西留斯喺一旁交談。]
passages.vernacularMandarin: [布魯圖斯與魯西留斯在一旁交談。]

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Messala.
passages.vernacular: 梅薩拉。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 梅薩拉。

passages.title: Messala 梅薩拉
passages.original: What says my General?
passages.vernacular: 將軍有乜嘢吩咐?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 將軍有什麼吩咐?

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Messala, This is my birth-day; as this very day Was Cassius born. Give me thy hand, Messala: Be thou my witness that against my will As Pompey was, am I compell’d to set Upon one battle all our liberties. You know that I held Epicurus strong, And his opinion. Now I change my mind, And partly credit things that do presage. Coming from Sardis, on our former ensign Two mighty eagles fell, and there they perch’d, Gorging and feeding from our soldiers’ hands, Who to Philippi here consorted us. This morning are they fled away and gone, And in their steads do ravens, crows, and kites Fly o’er our heads, and downward look on us, As we were sickly prey: their shadows seem A canopy most fatal, under which Our army lies, ready to give up the ghost.
passages.vernacular: 梅薩拉,今日係我嘅生日;卡修斯都正是喺呢一天出生。把你嘅手畀我,梅薩拉:你嚟作證,我像龐培一樣,係違背自己意願,被迫把我哋全部嘅自由押喺一場戰鬥上。你知道我曾堅信伊壁鳩魯同佢嘅睇法。而家我改變咗主意,有點相信嗰啲預兆。從薩迪斯嚟嘅時候,有兩隻巨大嘅老鷹落喺我哋嘅先頭旗上,牠哋棲喺嗰度,從我哋士兵手中吞食,一路陪我哋到呢度腓力比。今早牠哋已飛走唔見喇,取而代之嘅係烏鴉、渡鴉同鳶,喺我哋頭上飛翔,向下睇住我哋,好像我哋係生病嘅獵物:牠哋嘅影子像一頂最不祥嘅華蓋,我哋嘅軍隊躺喺其下,幾乎要斷氣。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 梅薩拉,今天是我的生日;卡修斯也正是在這一天出生。把你的手給我,梅薩拉:你來作證,我像龐培一樣,是違背自己意願,被迫把我們全部的自由押在一場戰鬥上。你知道我曾堅信伊壁鳩魯和他的看法。現在我改變了主意,有點相信那些預兆。從薩迪斯來的時候,有兩隻巨大的老鷹落在我們的先頭旗上,牠們棲在那裡,從我們士兵手中吞食,一路陪我們到這裡腓力比。今早牠們已飛走不見了,取而代之的是烏鴉、渡鴉和鳶,在我們頭上飛翔,向下看著我們,好像我們是生病的獵物:牠們的影子像一頂最不祥的華蓋,我們的軍隊躺在其下,幾乎要斷氣。

passages.title: Messala 梅薩拉
passages.original: Believe not so.
passages.vernacular: 唔好咁樣相信。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不要這樣相信。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: I but believe it partly, For I am fresh of spirit, and resolv’d To meet all perils very constantly.
passages.vernacular: 我都不過一半相信,因為我精神飽滿,決心堅定地面對一切危險。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 我也不過一半相信,因為我精神飽滿,決心堅定地面對一切危險。

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Even so, Lucilius.
passages.vernacular: 就咁樣,魯西留斯。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就這樣,魯西留斯。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Now, most noble Brutus, The gods today stand friendly, that we may, Lovers in peace, lead on our days to age! But, since the affairs of men rest still incertain, Let’s reason with the worst that may befall. If we do lose this battle, then is this The very last time we shall speak together: What are you then determined to do?
passages.vernacular: 而家,最高貴嘅布魯圖斯,願諸神今日對我哋友善,使我哋能夠作為和平中嘅朋友,一直活到老年!但係既然人間嘅事仍然不確定,讓我哋就最壞可能發生嘅事嚟推論一下。如果我哋輸咗呢場戰鬥,咁呢個就係我哋最後一次談話:咁你決定點做?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 現在,最高貴的布魯圖斯,願諸神今天對我們友善,使我們能夠作為和平中的朋友,一直活到老年!但是既然人間的事仍然不確定,讓我們就最壞可能發生的事來推論一下。如果我們輸了這場戰鬥,那麼這就是我們最後一次談話:那麼你決定怎麼做?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: Even by the rule of that philosophy By which I did blame Cato for the death Which he did give himself, I know not how, But I do find it cowardly and vile, For fear of what might fall, so to prevent The time of life, arming myself with patience To stay the providence of some high powers That govern us below.
passages.vernacular: 就按嗰套哲學嘅原則,我曾因為加圖自殺而責備佢,我唔知點解,但我發現為了害怕可能發生嘅事,就咁樣提前結束生命,係怯懦卑劣嘅;我要以耐心武裝自己,等待嗰統治我哋下界嘅某些高等力量嘅安排。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 就按那套哲學的原則,我曾因為加圖自殺而責備他,我不知為什麼,但我發現為了害怕可能發生的事,就這樣提前結束生命,是怯懦卑劣的;我要以耐心武裝自己,等待那統治我們下界的某些高等力量的安排。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: Then, if we lose this battle, You are contented to be led in triumph Thorough the streets of Rome?
passages.vernacular: 咁,如果我哋輸咗呢場戰鬥,你甘願被牽住喺羅馬嘅街道上凱旋遊行?
passages.vernacularMandarin: 那麼,如果我們輸了這場戰鬥,你甘願被牽著在羅馬的街道上凱旋遊行?

passages.title: Brutus 布魯圖斯
passages.original: No, Cassius, no: think not, thou noble Roman, That ever Brutus will go bound to Rome; He bears too great a mind. But this same day Must end that work the Ides of March begun; And whether we shall meet again I know not. Therefore our everlasting farewell take. For ever, and for ever, farewell, Cassius. If we do meet again, why, we shall smile; If not, why then this parting was well made.
passages.vernacular: 不,卡修斯,不:高貴嘅羅馬人,別以為布魯圖斯會被綁住回羅馬;佢嘅心太高傲。但就喺今日,必須結束三月十五日開始嘅嗰件事;我哋會唔會再見面,我唔知道。所以,請接受我哋永遠嘅告別。永遠,永遠,再見喇,卡修斯。如果我哋再見面,哈,我哋就微笑;如果不,咁呢次分別都算係好好告別喇。
passages.vernacularMandarin: 不,卡修斯,不:高貴的羅馬人,別以為布魯圖斯會被綁著回羅馬;他的心太高傲。但就在今天,必須結束三月十五日開始的那件事;我們會不會再見面,我不知道。所以,請接受我們永遠的告別。永遠,永遠,再見了,卡修斯。如果我們再見面,哈,我們就微笑;如果不,那麼這次分別也算是好好告別了。

passages.title: Cassius 卡修斯
passages.original: For ever and for ever farewell, Brutus. If we do meet again, we’ll smile indeed; If not, ’tis true this parting was well made.
passages.vernacular: 永遠,永遠,再見喇,布魯圖斯。如果我哋再見面,我哋就真嘅微笑;如果不,的確呢次分別係好好告別喇。
